datalab-68d50e85fb8de4fae0e0eafaf20e63c0.description: A diagram of a complete graph K4 with 4 vertices and 6 edges. The vertices are arranged in a diamond shape with one vertex in the center (though it's actually a planar projection of K4 where the 'center' is an intersection of two edges). The edges are colored to show a 3-edge coloring: the outer boundary edges are blue (top-left and bottom-right) and red (top-right and bottom-left), while the two crossing internal edges are yellow/gold.

datalab-f11b8f19a9a2518acf8ea2482a5579d2.description: Diagram of the Inverter gadget. It shows two pairs of horizontal lines representing edges. The input on the left consists of two red lines, labeled 'entrada: V' (true). An arrow points from these lines to a black rectangular box labeled 'inversor'. Another arrow points from the box to two output lines on the right, one red and one blue, labeled 'saída: F' (false).

datalab-1be8e9cad5f38fa47bdb81e549a3bec9.description: Diagram of a variable gadget. A black box labeled 'x' has three red lines extending from it to the right, labeled 'ocorrência 1', 'ocorrência 2', and 'ocorrência 3'.

datalab-43fec6623ab9cb223a9ff74e2d2a4402.description: Diagram of an inverter gadget. Two examples are shown. The first shows two red lines entering a black box labeled 'inversor' from the left, and two blue lines exiting to the right, labeled 'saída: F'. The second shows two blue lines entering the box, and two red lines exiting, labeled 'saída: V'. Below the boxes, the logic is summarized: 'V entra -> F sai | F entra -> V sai'.

datalab-c1c7af7ea36be0323047962df57d75b0.description: Green arrow pointing right, indicating the direction of the proof from satisfiability to 3-edge-coloring.

datalab-48d61f7cf40bacce4d63f9e98ea225fb.description: Red arrow pointing left, indicating the direction of the proof from 3-edge-coloring to satisfiability.

datalab-dbe553cf16dd14073b89a8263a428664.description: Diagrama conceitual da construção de G_Φ. Três gadgets de variável (x, y, z) e um inversor (¬y) estão conectados a um único gadget de cláusula C1. O gadget x está conectado ao gadget C1 por uma aresta rotulada 'literal x (positivo)'. O gadget y está conectado ao inversor (¬y) por uma aresta rotulada 'y'. O inversor (¬y) está conectado ao gadget C1 por uma aresta rotulada '¬y'. O gadget z está conectado ao gadget C1 por uma aresta rotulada 'literal z (positivo)'.

datalab-b8661c6c54f72ecc7ff6cb05e47b2891.description: Diagram illustrating the 3-edge-coloring of a clause gadget C1 for the formula Φ = (x ∨ ¬y ∨ z). The diagram shows three literals (x, y, z) connected to a clause gadget C1. Literal x is positive (x=V) and connects to a 'PAR x' box (mesma cor = V ✓). Literal y is negative (y=F) and connects to a 'PAR y' box (cores diff. = F ✓), which then connects to an 'inversor (¬y)' box (y=F → ¬y=V), which connects to a 'PAR ¬y' box (mesma cor = V ✓). Literal z is positive (z=V) and connects to a 'PAR z' box (mesma cor = V ✓). All three 'PAR' boxes connect to the clause gadget C1 (3-EDGE-COLORABLE ✓). A legend explains the edge colors: red for 'mesma cor → V', blue for 'cores diff. → F', and yellow for 'após inversor → V'.
